entries.description: Operator set pathAwareCritique: advisory.
Read spec, routed cut list, the three current tutorials, consumer-bootstrap templates, and the shipped command surface (package.json contributed commands, moduleAuthoring writers, copilot_catalog).

Resolved both named runtime unknowns EMPIRICALLY against shipped code: (a) renameModule restamps module: in starter specs + manifest slug/title only - folder names, planPath and codeRoots do NOT follow; fallback New Module + Delete Module probed and is clean. (b) Copilot CLI live 1.0.75 vs lock pin 1.0.69 = live version-pin drift; --model claude-sonnet-4.6 smoke test ran exit 0 on 1.0.75.

Routed step-3.5 analysis (gemini-2.5-pro, anthropic excluded, $0.0119, truncation-clean); ai-assignment.md authored. Verdict: authoring orchestrator-direct for fidelity, add a routed reader-simulation review before Step 7.

Authored docs/tutorials/hello-world.md - 264 lines, six parts 1:1 with six video scenes, solo-first with the explicit "Solo repositories can stop here." at the end of Part 4, GitHub + Copilot CLI worked path, ADO/direct-API inline variants, staged 3-stage branch protection, minimally-adapted scaffolded CI, five-item check, no appendices.

Authored docs/tutorials/release-and-recovery.md (154 lines) from the excised Part 10 + Git-under-the-hood appendix; all command literals re-verified against src/commands/gitRelease.ts and gitWorkflow.ts.
git rm the 821-line Copilot+ADO cut and the 390-line review prompt; module-team-hello-world.md reduced to the single one-line redirect stub.

Repaired inbound links in docs/quick-start.md, README.md, tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/README.md, and docs/module-reorganization.md. Remaining references are exactly the three files S2 owns (getting-started.md.template + two cold-start fixtures).
Confirmed zero surviving shared-spine / sync-map / every-echo / tutorial-pair obligations in docs/tutorials/. Teaching surface 1,968 -> 419 lines.

Layer 1 pytest: 3060 passed, 6 skipped. Extension unit suite (vscode-stub mocha): 1767 passing, 0 failing. Layer 3 Playwright not run - no Explorer-rendering, state-writer, or fixture change (L-064-12 triggers absent).
Routed pre-verification reader-simulation pass (gemini-2.5-pro, documentation, $0.0134): 2 blocking + 3 confusing findings, all five fixed before verification.

Phased discovery (gpt-5.6 x2 fan-out, $0.7276): ISSUES_FOUND, 11 blocking. Supplementary pass (gpt-5.6, $0.2849): 2 further blocking. All 13 accepted and remediated in one pass; sidecar s1-remediation-round-2.md written.

Remediation-review round 3 (gpt-5.6, $0.1257): 9 fix-accepted, 1 accepted-with-modification, 3 rejected. 2 of the 3 new Majors fixed (literal DABBLER_* names restored; ADO self-approval vote made explicit). 1 DISPUTED (R3-3: verifier prescribes shipping azure-pipelines.yml, which the operator-confirmed cut list forbids verbatim) - escalated to operator, not re-rounded. Sidecar s1-remediation-round-3.md written.

Committed (02a3212, d68c9e5, 8f5d026) and PUSHED. close_session REFUSED on the verification_backstop gate: OpenAI 429 across 4 verify_session attempts plus the backstop 2 tries; OpenAI holds the only tier-3 verifiers outside the orchestrator provider (anthropic), and google has no tier-3 verifier enabled, so the cross-provider fallback has nowhere to go. Session left in-flight for the operator: re-run close_session when the provider recovers. --manual-verify NOT self-authorized (operator-only). Notification NOT fired (fires only after a successful close).

Round 4 (gpt-5.6, $0.1192) after operator restored OpenAI funds: 14 fix-accepted, 1 accepted-with-modification, 1 rejected. The round-3 DISPUTED azure-pipelines.yml Major did NOT recur - the Part 2 scope-statement resolution was accepted, so that dispute is settled with no cut-list breach. One new Major (Node.js floor): its stated evidence was checked and is false (npm view @github/copilot -> engines: null), but the concern was real and was fixed by REMOVAL - winget list proved the walk machine runs the standalone GitHub.Copilot winget build with no Node at all, so the Node prerequisite was deleted and winget became the primary install. Same check also proved the CLI self-updates (winget records 1.0.51, binary reports 1.0.75), which is the mechanism behind the catalog pin drift; now taught explicitly. Remediation-review cap (2 cycles) REACHED - loop suspends, no further cycle self-authorized.

close_session backstop (round 5, gpt-5.6, $0.3160) found 1 blocking Major: release-and-recovery.md still used the broken direct-script invocation python services/app/app.py in two places - the sys.path defect fixed in hello-world.md at round 1 was never propagated to the sibling doc (an L-065-1 every-echo miss, mine). Both fixed to python -m services.app.app; grep -rn "python services/" docs/tutorials/ now returns nothing. Sidecar s1-remediation-round-5.md written.

Round 6 (gpt-5.6, $0.3897): 2 blocking Majors, both accepted, one shared root cause - the tutorial never said where the plan/decomposition sessions run once main is protected, nor how their output reaches main before the worktree is cut from it. Fixed with an authoring branch over Part 4 steps 1-2 plus a new step 3 that lands the plan and generated set via Open PR (Part 4 renumbered 1-10), and by moving the app prerequisite edit ahead of the authoring PR in Part 5. Sidecar s1-remediation-round-6.md written.

Round 7 (gpt-5.6, $0.3395): 1 blocking Major, accepted - round 6 fixed the authoring-branch requirement for Part 4 (greeter) but not Part 5 step 6 (Sam/app), so the team path still started its lifecycle sessions on protected main. Third L-065-1 every-echo miss this session. Fixed: Part 5 step 6 now opens with git switch -c authoring/app-lifecycle and the landing bullet names that branch and the return to trunk. Blocking-per-round: 11,2,3,1,1,2,1.

Round 8 (gpt-5.6, $0.4115): 2 Majors, neither closable by another round. R8-1 worktrees: kernel accepted (my prose over-claimed that no AI session touches the main checkout - sentence narrowed), remedy DISPUTED against cut list SS E step 7 / SS F. R8-2 size: 344 lines vs <=260 Ends-with, every line above the 269-line pre-verification draft added by verifier-demanded fixes; unresolvable without reversing Majors. Session STOPS to the operator per the constitution (unfixed/disputed Critical-Major goes to the human, never another round). Blocking-per-round 11,2,3,1,1,2,1,2. Verification spend ~$3.6. close_session correctly still refuses; NOT forced.

Round 9 (close backstop, gpt-5.6, $0.3650) returned VERIFIED on the first of the three operator-authorized rounds - --manual-verify was NOT needed. All six close gates PASSED (working_tree_clean, pushed_to_remote, activity_log_entry, next_orchestrator_present, change_log_fresh, verification_integrity). session-state.json flipped to complete/closed by the blessed writer; S1 verificationVerdict=VERIFIED. Total verification spend across 9 rounds: ~$4.0.
Registered session 2 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high); read the preload, the spec, S1's disposition, s1-runtime-unknowns.md, and the new docs/tutorials/hello-world.md.

Confirmed S1's Creates/Touches on disk: docs/tutorials/hello-world.md (314 lines), release-and-recovery.md, the redirect stub at module-team-hello-world.md, and both retired docs gone. Located S2's targets: the three consumer-bootstrap templates, the cold-start golden tree (test-fixtures/cold-start/{full,lightweight}/) and its regeneration mechanism (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm run test:unit).

Step 3.5: routed assignment analysis (gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0111) -> s2-ai-assignment-analysis.json; S2 block appended to ai-assignment.md. Step 2: re-cut CODEOWNERS.template from the three-person cast (greeter/clock/integration) to the tutorial's two-module cast, with the worked example reduced to exactly the two rule lines the tutorial tells the reader to uncomment (leading-slash form, matching hello-world.md Part 5 byte-for-byte). Dropped the plan-folder rules, the three-person touches narration, and the commented conflict-magnet rule pair (kept as one sentence).

Step 3: routed CI-template design analysis (gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0233) -> s2-ci-template-analysis.json. Adopted its job-name verdict (all-modules -> test, matching the tutorial's required-check name) and its pull_request finding (running the aggregate job on PRs strengthens the anti-integration-bomb guarantee). DECLINED its fail-closed placeholder - reasoning recorded in the disposition. Template cut 85 -> 42 lines; path-filter block reduced to a 4-line commented pointer.

Step 4: getting-started.md.template re-pointed to docs/tutorials/hello-world.md, review-prompt URL dropped, blurb re-cut from 'three people, three modules ... tags' to the solo-first shape; added one clause on what Rename Module does and does not carry (S1's empirical finding), which the old text tacitly contradicted. Regenerated both cold-start goldens via the sanctioned UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 path; rebuilt dist/templates via npm run compile.

Step 3b: proved green-on-empty by execution -> s2-green-on-empty-proof.md. Structure check establishes the run block is the only repo-contributed failure surface; the block then ran under bash -e in a fresh empty git repo (exit 0, wrote nothing); parity check confirms template == both goldens == dist copy. All 18 checks PASS; the three things it cannot prove locally are named.

Step 5: extension 0.45.0 -> 0.46.0 with a template-bundle-only CHANGELOG section; publish left un-run (no tag, no publish). Router-side confirmed a NO-OP: this session touched zero files under ai_router/, so dabbler-ai-router stays 0.33.0 rather than being bumped for symmetry - stated in the CHANGELOG rather than left implicit. Recorded the staged version in docs/repository-reference.md's canonical release-status table (scope note: not in the spec's Touches list; added because that table is the canonical home for release facts and would otherwise claim 0.45.0 while package.json says 0.46.0).

Full suite GREEN across all three layers. Layer 1 pytest: 3060 passed, 6 skipped (395s). Layer 2 extension unit suite via the shipped vscode-stub mocha path: 1767 passing, 0 failing (incl. consumerBootstrap.test.ts, coldStartSnapshot.test.ts, gettingStartedActions.test.ts, gitScaffoldCore.test.ts). Layer 3 Playwright run because this session regenerated the cold-start fixture tree (L-064-12): 28 passed (7.8m), incl. vsix-first-run-walkthrough.

Verification closed VERIFIED. Round 1 discovery (fan-out 2/2, gpt-5-6, $0.3425): VERIFIED, 0 blocking, 3 nits - all fixed. --phase remediation-review then correctly refused (round 1 recorded no findings, so there is no discovery baseline to review a fix delta against); ran a second discovery pass instead, which is the honest way to cover bytes changed after a verified round. Round 2 discovery (fan-out 2/2, gpt-5-6, $0.2895): VERIFIED, 0 blocking, 5 nits - all fixed, no round 3 opened (two discovery passes is the bound; Minor-only is effectively VERIFIED; L-095-1). Total verification cost $0.632. Final suite re-run on the shipped tree: pytest 3060 passed/6 skipped, extension unit 1767 passing, Playwright 28 passed.
Registered S3 (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high); read the preload, the spec, S1+S2 dispositions, s1-runtime-unknowns.md, and docs/tutorials/hello-world.md end to end as a reader would.

Routed step-3.5 assignment analysis (analysis, anthropic excluded -> gemini-2.5-pro, $0.0098, truncation-clean); appended the S3 block to ai-assignment.md. Analyst returned orchestrator-direct for all four authoring steps; its clean-environment desk-check control declined with reasons (it IS the S4 walk) and replaced by four cheaper controls.

Authored docs/tutorials/video/ — 9 files, 1,952 lines: README (scene order, variant matrix, runtime estimates, OBS scenes/sources, the must-never-be-on-screen checklist, the beat format) + six scene scripts 1:1 with the tutorial parts. Every beat carries Do / Say / See, cites its tutorial step in a per-file traceability table, and adds an "If this fails on camera" line wherever a known failure mode exists (Copilot auth, CLI version pin drift, branch protection on GitHub Free, red CI, finalize refusals). Async beats are marked WAIT with a duration; take boundaries are marked CUT.

Authored the two alternate takes: scene-1-alt-direct-api (replaces scene 1; names its 3 downstream changes and its rejoin point; keys set OFF CAMERA with a presence-only probe) and scene-2-alt-azure-devops (replaces scene 2; names its 5 downstream beat substitutions and its rejoin point; scratch-org warning).

Fixed three things in docs/tutorials/hello-world.md that scripting exposed. Two were S2-queued residuals in Part 4 step 6 (a stale "delete any if: line" clause that is a no-op after S2 re-cut the template, and prose that undersold the CI edit by two steps) — fixed together by rewriting the sentence to the real add-two-steps-replace-one-run-block edit and renaming the printed step to the scaffolded "Build and test every module", so the edit really is add-only. The third is NEW and is the more serious: Part 5 step 6 promised the app implementation set "shows as blocked in the Work Explorer" — but blockedMarker() suppresses on a SATISFIED prerequisite, and greeter is already complete at that point, so the reader would look for a marker that can never appear. Rewritten to say nothing changes on screen, and why.

Authored 106-hello-world-tutorial-simplification-uat-checklist.json — 13 walks to the Set 078 bar. Walks 1-10 follow the tutorial Part 1 -> Part 6 in its natural order with no reordering; walks 11-12 are the alternate-take spot checks, flagged INTENTIONALLY out of order in both Subarea and HumanAction; walk 13 is the whole-script attestation. Every walk opens with a "Where you are" preamble, carries literal copy-pasteable HumanAction steps and literal-string Expectations, and names the scene script it dry-runs. 10 items declare ProgrammaticVerification, 3 declare NoProgrammaticPathReason.

Ran two committed mechanical gates instead of the routed analyst-proposed clean-environment desk check (declined with reasons — it IS the S4 walk). s3-check-literals.py: 98/98 PASS (command titles resolve to real contributed commands; 44 shared literals identical; CI YAML byte-identical tutorial<->scene 4 and add-only from the scaffolded template; all relative links resolve). s3-check-checklist.py: 345/345 PASS (schema shape; the ad-hoc UAT floor; the 078 authoring bar). Evidence: s3-authoring-gates.md, which also names the five things the gates do NOT establish.

Full suite on the reviewed tree: Layer 1 pytest 3060 passed / 6 skipped (410.82s, exit 0); Layer 2 npx tsc --noEmit clean + npm run test:unit 1767 passing. Layer 3 Playwright deliberately NOT run — L-064-12 arms it for Explorer-rendering surfaces, state-file writers, or the fixture harness, and this session changes none of them (markdown under docs/tutorials/ plus one session-set JSON artifact).

Round 1 discovery (fan-out 2/2, gpt-5-6, $0.7013): ISSUES_FOUND, 18 blocking. Round 2 supplementary completeness critic run BEFORE any remediation per the loop discipline (gpt-5-6, $0.3002): 2 more blocking. The fan-out duplicated 5, so the merged harvest is 15 distinct defects. All 15 accepted; none disputed.

Fixed all 15 in one pass across 10 files; sidecar s3-remediation-round-3.md. The dominant class was a step that cannot be performed from the state the previous step leaves behind -- both authoring gates were green while all 15 were live, which is exactly the limitation s3-authoring-gates.md names about itself. 7 of the 15 touched hello-world.md under the spec's scripting-exposed-gap clause, each listed individually in the sidecar so the judgment can be audited. Extended s3-check-literals.py so the 4 most drift-prone fixes cannot silently re-open: 104/104 PASS (was 98/98); checklist gate 345/345 PASS; extension unit re-run 1767 passing.

Cycle 1 (round 3, gpt-5-6, $0.1785): 13 accepted / 1 accepted-with-modification / 2 rejected. Both rejections were the Azure DevOps take: Walk 11 was a spot check that never exercised the newly added Azure CLI install while Walk 13 attested every script followable, and fix N had WEAKENED the private-repos-never-on-screen rule instead of satisfying it. Fixed by making Walk 11 a full beat 1-6 execution, scoping Walk 13's claim to walked-vs-reviewed, and making the ADO scratch project PUBLIC (org policy toggle scripted, hard stop if unavailable) so the README's rule is restored unconditional.

Cycle 2 (round 4, gpt-5-6, $0.1855): 15 of 16 accepted, 1 rejected -- fix A had swapped one unavailable dependency for another (a future recorder has no way to obtain the 0.46.0 VSIX the scene now told them to sideload). Accepted and fixed BY REMOVAL: both scene-1 takes drop the sideload branch for a recording precondition (do not record until the Marketplace is at 0.46.0 -- a video must show a path a viewer can follow), and the VSIX stays only in the S4 walk, named in both places as the one deliberate departure from a scene script. THE BOUNDED TOTAL OF 2 REMEDIATION-REVIEW CYCLES IS NOW REACHED: the loop suspends and the session stops to the operator for adjudication rather than opening cycle 3. Convergence across four rounds: 18 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 blocking, acceptance 13/16 -> 15/16, zero findings disputed, nothing reopened.

Operator ruled at the bound: one more cycle, then a third-provider opinion, then close. Cycle 3 (round 5, gpt-5-6, $0.1583): VERIFIED, ZERO findings, 16 accepted / 0 rejected / 1 accepted-with-modification. Same-provider loop closed 18 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0.

Routed the full 198k-char evidence bundle to google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview ($0.0745, truncation-clean) — the one provider family neither the orchestrator (anthropic) nor any of the five rounds (openai) had used. Verdict ISSUES_FOUND, convergence_assessment.genuine FALSE. Found a Critical five rounds walked past: gh auth login writes ONE credential per OS user and Open PR runs gh pr create, so on the one-machine two-person staging every PR Sam opens would be authored by Priya — she could not approve it and CODEOWNERS would never request her, dead-ending Walks 8 and 9 and emptying scene 6 beat 2. Plus one Minor (checklist flattened cross-platform commands to Windows). It challenged NONE of the 19 prior fixes. Both accepted and fixed in the STAGING only (scene 5 note + beats 3/8/12, scene 6 beat 1, Walks 7/8/9, Notes PLATFORM para); the tutorial is untouched because it is correct — real Priya and Sam are on their own machines. Literal gate extended to pin gh auth status: 107/107 PASS; checklist gate 345/345; extension unit 1767 passing. Artifact: s3-third-provider-opinion.md.
Full disposition authored preserving the patched verification fields (api / VERIFIED). Session cost $1.6081 across 7 routed calls.

close_session gate failed on the Set 084 close backstop: its in-process round 6 (gpt-5-6, $0.3545) found 1 Major that only shows when the scripts are read as a SYSTEM — five authentication beats said to switch OBS to "a scene that hides the device code" while the README defined four scenes, all capture scenes. Fixed by defining a fifth OBS scene, Privacy (no capture at all), naming it literally in all five beats, switching BEFORE the credential appears, and declaring it per script; three stale beat references corrected in the same pass. Round 7 ($0.1830): 18/18 prior fixes accepted, 1 new Major created by the fix itself (scene 5 beat 3 gh auth login did not name Privacy) — fixed and closed on orchestrator judgment per the operator ruling rather than another round. Gates: 107/107 and 345/345.

close_session backstop rounds 8 and 10 each found real Majors, all fixed (fail-closed Passes, the az identity sibling and its own wrong first fix, and the uncommitted prerequisite). The final close attempt is blocked NOT on quality but on provider availability: OpenAI returned 429 Too Many Requests on three consecutive backstop attempts (3 retries each), and the gate correctly treats provider unavailability at close as a BLOCK, never a pass. All work is committed and pushed (9670797). Resolvable by re-running close_session when OpenAI recovers, or by the operator-attested --manual-verify path — both operator decisions. Notification deliberately NOT fired: it fires only after a successful close.
